request.spec:
A name or alias may no longer be used on a sheet when any sheet of its tree (its ancestors, its
descendants and their descendants, among the sheets that exist) already uses it as a name or alias:
adding, renaming, an alias, the quick-add bar, the paste box (and any later import) are refused as a
duplicate would be. People who already clash are not changed: each shows clashing yes, and every
edit of them through the person form is refused until the edit renames them to a name that does not
clash (and leaves no clashing alias).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A name or alias may no longer be used on a sheet when any sheet of its tree (its ancestors, its
descendants and their descendants, among the sheets that exist) already uses it as a name or alias:
adding, renaming, an alias, the quick-add bar, the paste box (and any later import) are refused as a
duplicate would be. People who already clash are not changed: each shows clashing yes, and every
edit of them through the person form is refused until the edit renames them to a name that does not
clash (and leaves no clashing alias).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
A name or alias is now refused when any other sheet in the sheet's tree already uses it, and people who already clash show `clashing` yes. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 acceptance tests.

**What counts as the tree:** the sheet's parent, that sheet's parent and so on up, plus its children, their children and so on down, counting only sheets that exist. I didn't include siblings (other children of the sheet's parent), because I read "its descendants and their descendants" as the sheet's own descendants. The tests don't cover a sibling case, so if you meant siblings to count, it's a small change in `PersonRepository.treeOf`.

**Server changes:**
- **Duplicate check:** `PersonRepository.nameTaken` now also looks at names and aliases on the other sheets in the tree. Adding a person, renaming and adding an alias all use it, so they're refused the same way a duplicate on the same sheet is. The error message now reads "…in use on this sheet or another sheet of its tree".
- **Quick-add:** when the typed name isn't on the sheet but another sheet in the tree uses it, quick-add is refused instead of creating a new person.
- **Paste box:** no change needed. It already refuses names that aren't on the sheet.
- **Editing a clashing person:** the person form refuses the edit unless the new name doesn't clash. It also refuses if one of the person's aliases clashes, since the form can't change aliases; that person can never be edited through the form.
- **Transfer:** the target sheet's whole tree is checked now, leaving out the person being moved so they don't clash with themselves.
- **Clashing flag:** each person in the API response now carries `clashing`. It's always worked out against the current data of the other sheets, including when you view the sheet as of a past date. That's because the past-date snapshot only holds this sheet's own data.

**Front end:** a new "Clashing" column (`person-clashing`) next to the aliases shows yes or no.

Setting a parent that creates new clashes is still allowed, as the request says: the people involved are left as they are and just show as clashing.
